source.value:
To get the normal equation corresponding to $W\!A\mathbf{x}=W\mathbf{b},$ we pre-multiply both sides of the equation by $(W\!A)^T{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}(W\,A)^{T}\cdot W\,Ax & =(W\,A)^{T}\cdot Wb \\ {A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)Ax & ={A}^{T}({W}^{T}W)b\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14073770/assets/f7cc4573dd79ddd8b872f75bae85670e72dcdcba0b2a514d9e21a27c599fc711.png)

our normal equation can be written as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 \\ 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 9\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 3\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 4 \\ 9 & 18\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 2\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ 0 \\ 27\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}10 & 18 \\ 18 & 40\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}29 \\ 54\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
a+b+c=10+40+54 = 104.
$$

Now, we solve the system corresponding to the above matrix equation using Gaussian elimination, as follows:
